title: Meta-analysis: in vivo passive lumbar flexion stiffness per quartile of range of motion (weighted mean, 95% CI)
condition: passive (relaxed, EMG-verified in source studies), healthy adults

quantity.name: through-range passive flexion stiffness
quantity.definition: participant-weighted mean of study stiffness values (slope of passive moment vs lumbar angle) assigned to quartiles of the maximum passive ROM (studies limited to e.g. 70% ROM rescaled to 100%; low/transition/high zones mapped to quartiles); 95% CI from SD of study means

source.authors: Watt AA, Callaway AJ, Williams JM
source.sample: meta-analysis of 13 in vivo studies (1994-2021), 354 relevant participants in total; synthesis restricted to control/baseline adults with mean age < 60 (study mean ages 21.0-30.3 y)

protocol.summary: Systematic review/meta-analysis (search Feb 2022). 8 of 10 flexion studies side-lying with legs/pelvis fixed and trunk on a frictionless platform; 2 standing (Shojaei 2018, Toosizadeh 2012). Source studies used EMG passivity thresholds from >2% to >5% MVC or baseline-based criteria.
how_to_simulate: Set the model to the posture of the source tests (flexion: side-lying with pelvis and legs fixed, trunk supported frictionlessly; see individual tests) with all muscle activations zero (passive muscle force-length only)
Impose lumbar flexion from neutral to the model's maximum passive range in small steps, distributing rotation over the lumbar joints as in the model's passive kinematics
Compute the total passive moment about the lumbosacral reference (L5-S1 / pelvis, i.e. the moment needed at the trunk-pelvis interface) and its slope vs lumbar angle
Average the slope within each quartile of the model's maximum ROM and compare with the weighted mean (pass if inside the 95% CI)
protocol.notes: META-ANALYSIS: pooled values are derived from underlying studies, some of which are also individual tests in this bench; never pool these with the individual studies (see underlying_studies). Studies in synthesis for this plane: De Carvalho & Callaghan 2011 (n=20, side-lying); Gruevski & Callaghan 2019 (n=34, side-lying (young cohort only relevant: 17)); McGill 1994 (n=37, side-lying); Shojaei 2018 (n=20, standing); Tennant 2020 (n=71, side-lying); Voinier 2020 (n=31, side-lying (controls only relevant)). Also reviewed: Beach 2005 [2], Fewster 2021 [5], Lee & McGill 2017 [9], Toosizadeh 2012 [18] (not in the quantitative synthesis).

extraction.check_notes: All quartile means and CI bounds re-read from pdftotext of Table 5; study lists from Results 3.1-3.3 and reference list.

pass_rule.rule: model quartile stiffness within the 95% CI (quartiles 3-4 of axial rotation: within +-50% of mean)
